question_type: seven-year agency series stitched from multiple issues (latest vintage per year) -> mean YoY growth + log-linear OLS slope/intercept with an index-origin convention
decisive_step: Three decisions: (i) table FFO-3 'On-Budget and Off-Budget Outlays by Agency', column 'Judicial branch (2)' (reference worklog Step 3-4, treasury_bulletin_2013_12.txt:736-746), rejecting the FFO-4 fund-group sum that differs by one unit in FY2013 (worklog Step 5 'dead end'); (ii) latest vintage per fiscal year, which requires several issues because each FFO-3 printing carries only ~5 actual years (FY2007 last printed in 2012_09:725, FY2008 in 2013_09:713; revisions to FY2007/2008/2009/2011 after first print; worklog Step 5); (iii) regressing ln(outlays) on a 1-based fiscal-year index (FY2007 = 1), which fixes the intercept while the slope is convention-free (worklog 'Decision on index'; review.md check 5). All four cells made all three the same way.

a.path_summary: find_tables 'Judicial Branch on-budget off-budget outlays' -> FFO-3 (a[4]); show_table on the latest issue showed the table starts in 2020 (a[10]); printings --table FFO-3 --row FY2007..FY2013 --col 'Judicial branch' (a[12],[14]) printed per-year vintage summaries ('2 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS ... latest printing 2012_09') from which it took the latest values; calc at a[16],[18],[20] computed the mean YoY and OLS for index 1..7, 0..6 and the calendar year, and it chose 1..7 (a[21]). Then it fell into a two-command loop (relative-path sed exit 1 / absolute-path sed exit 0) repeated 46 times (a[24]-[206]), was compacted, and answered from the summary (a[207]).

alternatives.change: One sentence for regressions on an index: 'When a question says to regress on a "year index" or "time index" without defining it, compute with the first year = 1 (also print 0-based and the calendar-year fit) and answer the 1-based intercept unless the question defines the index.'

Risk: if a future question intends 0-based, the sentence could hurt - hence not first.

notes: 1) This question is the positive case for the printings tool: its per-row vintage summary ('2 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS across printings; <v1>: <issues>; <v2>: <issues>; latest printing <issue>') is exactly the multi-issue stitching the v8 arms had to do by hand, and it turned a 7-issue extraction into one loop of 7 calls. Keep that output format in v10. 2) Every cell hit 'show_table --grep Judicial -> 0 rows' because agencies are columns in FFO-3; a hint that the term matches a column label would save a call. 3) Cell a's loop is the same pathology as on question 005 and as v8-prompt on this question: a failing relative path alternated with the absolute path; the 'Loops' sentence in AGENTS.md has no effect on it, so the loop guard belongs in controls, not text. 4) b, b2 and c all trimmed printings output with tail -n 8; the summary lines happen to be at the end, which is why this worked - v10 should keep the summary last (or add --summary) so trimming keeps the decisive lines. 5) Ambiguities the cells resolved uniformly and correctly: arithmetic mean of 6 YoY rates (not CAGR), values in millions as printed, 1-based index.
